transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

It is most often airflow restriction, so let’s check the filters first as they are frequently clogged with fluff. Please switch off and unplug the machine, then remove and rinse the lint filter from the door opening under a tap. Also take out the condenser unit behind the bottom flap, rinse it thoroughly to clear any fine dust or fluff, and let it drip dry before refitting. Once both are clean and completely dry, try a normal cycle again to see if that improves the drying time.

ok did both. door filter had fluff and a waxy film, rinsed it till water went through. condenser was never cleaned and the front was matted with lint, came clean with the shower head. will run a cycle now

That is excellent progress and likely sorted the airflow issue. While you run that cycle, please check if your laundry was spun well in the washer, as very wet clothes can take much longer to dry. Also ensure the drum is no more than two-thirds full so the air can circulate freely around the items. If they are still damp after this cycle with a normal programme, we will look at other possibilities like the moisture sensors or settings.
Cycle finished. Clothes dried in about 100 minutes and the water container is nearly full. It was a normal-sized load and the spin was 1200, so that's all as usual.

That is great news and suggests the blockage was indeed the main culprit. Since the machine is now collecting water effectively, we can rule out drainage issues. The next most common cause for damp clothes is fabric conditioner coating the moisture sensors inside the drum. Please switch off and unplug the dryer, then locate the two metal strips near the lint filter housing and wipe them with a damp cloth to remove any residue. This simple check often restores proper drying performance if sensor sensitivity was being affected.
Ok, I looked at the bars in the drum and they were slightly dull, so I wiped them with vinegar. Anything else I should do?

You have done all the essential maintenance checks perfectly, so let’s look at how you are using it next. A common cause of damp clothes is selecting a programme with a lower dryness setting or a shorter time than needed for that load size. Please ensure you are using a standard cotton drying programme and check if your machine has a "sensor dry" option rather than a timed one. If the problem persists after trying a full sensor cycle, we can look at other possibilities like the vent hose or internal airflow.
